correctness.rationale: Pairwise heavy-count smoothing strictly decreases sum of squared heavy counts and weakly decreases majorization, because attainable pair differences retain parity and their nonnegative centers decrease by twice the integer ratio. Unit-item marginal increments are convexly ordered, so water-filling minimizes every separable convex sum for the balanced baselines. The resulting vector is globally majorization minimal, with explicitly calculated three-case load profile. A nearest-odd integer gives the strict nonintegral-ratio counterexample. A standalone exact test exhaustively checked 2,127,810 small allocations; it is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Provides exact majorization rather than merely one social-welfare optimum, a single simultaneously optimal allocation for all symmetric Schur-concave scores, an explicit exponent-compressed load formula with only constant binary arithmetic, and an if-and-only-if arithmetic boundary for a natural two-stage algorithm. The comparison with compact p-mean approximation and wider bi-valued algorithms motivates exactly why this structure is useful.
